title: Architectural review board approves 429 Gley Avenue porch project as submitted
text:
← Back to the wire

Architectural review board approves 429 Gley Avenue porch project as submitted
A board member questioned whether a new engaged pilaster would overlap the trim of a door and window before the design team clarified the spacing would hold.
The architectural review board approved plans for a new front porch stoop at 429 Gley Avenue during a meeting held Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026.
THE CONCERN A board member raised questions about discrepancies between the rendering and the hardline drawing for the project, presented by Meg Blaze of Hercules Design Build. "I have some questions about apparent discrepancies between the rendering and the hardline drawing," the board member said, noting the rendering showed only one window to the right of the porch when there are two existing. The board member said the rendering showed generous space between the porch and door trim, "however, when I look at the hardline drawing, it looks like that engaged column is going to overlap the window and door trim."
THE CLARIFICATION Blaze explained there is currently 7 and 3/4 inches between the door casing and window casing, and the column is 7 inches wide, so "it'll nestle right in there." Blaze said the engaged pilaster is structurally necessary because there is only a small amount of wall between the door and window where light switches are located, leaving no other place to put them. Blaze also said the beam height was reduced slightly so the top of the trim would align with the top of the door, which is about five inches wide, adding there is "a little bit of play" and it "is not going to interact with the door at all."
THE RESPONSE The board member said, "I appreciate that clarification. I just, you know, wanted to be sure because I'm sure we can kind of visualize how a miss or overlap would look and it would be painful."
OUTCOME After discussing the trim and skirting details, a board member said there were no further clarifications needed and moved to approve 429 Gley Avenue as submitted. The motion was seconded and passed, with one member opposed.
